item.title: [Level1Techs Forum] External SSD Suddenly Failing on DietPi (RPi5)
item.description:
Just posting this on the chance someone might have some relevant experience or knowledge.

For some time (two years, I think) I’ve had a Pi 5 running DietPi and some services including NZBGet, with NZBGet using an external 1TB Crucial X8 drive for storage. It all worked fine until this evening when I found that I couldn’t access the shared media drive from my desktop.

I SSH’d into the Pi and the drive wasn’t visible. I pulled the drive and plugged it into my desktop and everything looked fine. I then plugged it back into the Pi and it showed up and worked for a while but then disappeared again. I’ve repeated the check on my desktop and the drive still looks okay. I’ve also tried swapping the power supply for the Pi from the previous one (which was the official Pi5 PSU) to a more powerful PSU and the same problem occurs.

I guess it’s possible that the Pi USB hardware has failed in some way, but it still seems to recognise other devices. The obvious next step for me is to try a fresh Pi OS install and see what happens but I can’t get to that right now so I thought I’d just float the issue on th forum and see if anyone had ideas.

item.description:
I had already been doing some research into IA-64 when something suddenly caught my attention:

[5-bit Template][41-bit Slot 0][41-bit Slot 1][41-bit Slot 2]

There is something strangely adorable about this instruction bundle layout, so I started wondering: what would happen if I used it to visualize network traffic?

That thought eventually turned into this little desktop widget, and I wanted to share it with you.

P.S. This only maps network telemetry into an IA-64-inspired bundle format. It does not fully emulate or execute IA-64 instructions.

And. It reads Windows network-interface counters and does not inspect packet contents.

item.title: [V2EX] [Apple] 教大家如何申请豁免中国大陆地区 App Store ICP 备案
item.description:
最近各种 Agent Vibe Coding 很火，看到很多 V 友都在写 App 。

App 过审后，如果要在中国大陆分发，需要有 ICP 备案号。偶尔会出现首个版本没备案也没被拦，但后面还是有几率被拦掉。

如果你的 App 不联网，或者虽然联网，但只连接 Apple 的服务器使用 iOS 系统服务（如，连接苹果服务器完成 App 内购买），是可以向苹果申请豁免 ICP 备案的。否则都需要备案，不能豁免。

当然备案本身也不复杂，速度还可能更快，只是会有些额外的金钱和维护成本。

具体申请豁免的方法是：

1. https://developer.apple.com/cn/ ，拉到最底下“联系我们”；
2. 有新的问题 - 查看主题；
3. 分发 - 有关分发的其它疑问；
4. 填表。注意表格里“应用的 Apple ID”，指的是你 Connect 后台 App 信息里这个 App 的 Apple ID ，不是你自己的苹果账户 ID ；
5. 重现步骤写无，底下信息栏里说明，这款 App 无需联网，联网权限仅用于连接 IAP 购买（这里按实际情况写），申请豁免 ICP 备案；
6. 等苹果邮件。一般第二天会联系你提供材料，需要写一份声明，内容基本还是上面的这些信息。回复后通常就能豁免了。

大家一定要合规申请，如果确实有网络服务提供，还是要按规定备案的。

item.title: [V2EX] [OpenAI] chatgpt(codex)桌面端僵尸进程
item.description:
最近升级 codex 后，电脑经常崩溃，谷歌浏览器闪退，甚至终端都打不开，显示：
[forkpty: Resource temporarily unavailable]
[未能创建新的进程和打开伪终端(pseudo-tty)。]
似乎是无资源可用，只能重启电脑，重启后又好了。一开始以为电脑系统出问题了，没与 codex 联想起来。
今天又出现后，让 codex 去排查，得出的结果：

-------------------------------------------
我查到崩溃报告里的关键原因：
SkyComputerUseService
bundleID: com.openai.sky.CUAService
built for macOS 14.4 which is newer than running OS
Library not loaded: /usr/lib/swift/libswiftObservation.dylib
你的系统是：
macOS 13.6
所以现在情况是：
ChatGPT 主 app 自己标的是最低 macOS 12.0 ，所以它能打开。
但里面的 SkyComputerUseService 这个 helper 是按 macOS 14.4+ 构建的。
macOS 13.6 没有 libswiftObservation.dylib 。
helper 一启动就崩。
ChatGPT 又不停重试启动它。
每次失败留下 <defunct>，所以 ps aux | wc -l 持续上涨。
关闭 ChatGPT 后父进程退出，zombie 被系统回收，所以数量回到 400 多。
这不是你配置错了，也不是你没点“安装”的问题，是 当前 ChatGPT/Codex 版本的 Computer Use helper 和 macOS 13.6 不兼容，而且 app 没有正确停止重试。
最稳的解决方案：
升级 macOS 到 14.4 或更高。
如果暂时不想升级系统，就不要开 ChatGPT 桌面端里的 Codex/Computer Use 相关页面太久。
保留 /Applications/ChatGPT.app ，移走 /Applications/Codex.app ，避免双 bundle 干扰。
向 OpenAI 反馈时直接给这句：
SkyComputerUseService built for macOS 14.4 crashes on macOS 13.6 due to missing libswiftObservation.dylib, ChatGPT repeatedly restarts it and leaks zombie processes.
-------------------------------------------
用 ps aux | wc -l 查看进程数，10 分钟不到从 500 飙到 900 多了，估计得升级系统了

item.title: [Level1Techs Forum] AMD Pro r9700, CachyOS, and Sleep Bug
item.description:
Hello Community,

I recently made the leap to Linux and decided on CachyOS for performance reasons, and my desire to learn and troubleshoot with the command line. That said, when I put my PC to sleep, the screens darkened, but the PC fans stayed on (including RGB), and my GPU fans ramped up which was sustained. Upon some internet searches I read that this is a known bug with the AMDGPU kernel driver’s suspend/resume sequence, so I tried the Cachy OS LTS kernel with the same result.

Has anyone found a fix to this? I figured there have to be a number of you running CachyOS (or an Arch-based distro) with AMD GPUs, specifically r9700s.

Here are my specs:

TR 9960x
TRX50 AI TOP
6.18.42-1 Cachy LTS
64 GB 7200cl34
Gigabyte PRO r9700
Gigabyte AIC with two 1 tb Samsung 980s

Things I have done:

1). Identified it was a known bug with a likely root cause from the AMDGPU kernel driver’s suspend/resume sequence
2). Switching to CachyOS LTS kernel, no fix

Things I am considering:

1). Enabling Hibernate so I have a sleep like state that doesn’t require powering down
2). I read that the issue pertains to the GPU and NVME drivers suspending at the same time and an issue with the VRAM eviction. But that’s something that I’d want to learn more about before I go tinkering with those processes.
3). Going back to the 7.1.6-1 kernel since the LTS 6.1.42-1 did not solve the issue.

Any feedback would be helpful, thank you!

item.title: [Level1Techs Forum] Suggestions for shared VM hypervisor interoperable with VMWare Workstation on laptops
item.description:
Hi. I’m trying to improve my team’s virtualisation setup - we all use VMWare Workstation on our Windows laptops to run a bunch of Windows VMs with oddball software packages that can be finicky with hardware changes. At the moment there’s a lot of passing VMs around on USB drives, and getting lost in updated software versions within VMs, or the VM contents drifting from ‘golden image’ milestones.

I’d like to set up a central hypervisor that we can upload VMs from our laptops, so we can get:

  • a canonical ‘known-good’ VM version for each software with snapshotting/clones as software versions are updated in the VM
  • the ability to run up a VM for a quick test without waiting to move them around
  • BACKUPS

But.. the software installed in the VMs can have problems if the hardware changes, so I’m trying to find a way of modifying the virtual hardware as little as possible when uploading or downloading to the server.

VMware Workstation is used on laptops because it’s been the most reliable for USB passthrough, and I don’t like my chances of getting everyone to change the central piece of software they use for work.

Any suggestions for hypervisors or workflows that might smooth the process of shifting VMs back and forth?

item.title: [Level1Techs Forum] Looking for the best RAID option for a small personal NAS
item.description:
Hi! I’m new around here and want to hear second opinions. I’m a long time user of Linux/Unix for many years (not too heavy of a sysadmin, but I still know my way around decently).

I’m wanting to find a sweet spot for said NAS, and that sweet spot is a decent enough interface for regular users (since the rest of my family isn’t *nix inclined), but doesn’t abstract itself away too much to the point that if I need to dig into the guts it isn’t a massive pain in the back.

Just a Jellyfin, web-attached storage, and incremental backup to single-disk via a simple button is all I need – so a one-click Bash script or something that backs up to x disk UUID/ZFS pool or whatever should suffice.

The aforementioned single backup disk is primarily offline, so it shouldn’t be treated as a persistent piece of infrastructure, which was a big pain spot in the past on TrueNAS for me. I don’t know if I was just missing something there, but when I tried it a few years back it was really annoying to work with for this use case, and it felt like the UI didn’t accommodate for a disk only being attached for a short period of time.

My current setup is a copyparty instance pointed to a local 3x4TB BtrFS RAID 1 on Ubuntu, being backed up to a single 8TB disk using Borg Backup. Until very recently, I was using mdadm to accomplish the RAID, but it ended up being very unreliable and each reboot I had to constantly reconstruct the array manually despite having tried many things to get it mounting consistently on its own.

I’m thinking, considering my past experiences and current setup, the best balance between effort, storage space, reliability, safety, and ease of maintenance is using the existing OS installation with OpenZFS to make a RAID5 and back up either to the same Borg repository or via Syncoid. But maybe there’s something critical I was missing about TrueNAS in the past that would have made it perfect. I’d like to hear your experiences and wisdom.

item.title: [V2EX] [程序员] 我刚刚骂了 codex，然后感觉，它开始故意给我出岔子
item.description:
我起了个项目，代码已经写了可能几万行了， 现在让它补写项目愿景、开发规范、和下一步计划

特意使用了 5.6-sol Ultra 模式，

结果后它给我写了一坨，像是免责声明的东西，罗列了各种列表……我看了几段，感觉头皮发麻。

我重新修改了一下提示，让它不必巨细无遗，只说纲要、具有指导性的就行……

然后它又生成了风格还是一样的东西，几乎没变，然后我发彪了，让他在我之前手动写的版上改：

我靠，这是把我前面认为不合格，重做的那版又恢复了？？？真是浪费我 token!!!
你写的这个，是给人看的吗？我一看就头疼。。能说人话？，你要是给人介绍这个项目，会这样来说？？？？

撤销吧，在原版的基础框架上修订！

这个对话继续进行，但发现有些我觉得不说也可以对齐，不会有问题的，它偏偏就不往我想要的方向去，硬要我明确指出，感觉对话很费劲，，

我很快放弃了这个对话，开了个新的，和它说话的声音也变小了。。。
